lines.text: Linagliptin is used to treat type 2 diabetes.

Type 2 diabetes happens when your body does not make enough of a hormone called insulin, or the insulin it makes does not work properly (insulin resistance). Without enough insulin, your blood sugar (glucose) can get too high.
Linagliptin works by increasing the amount of insulin your body produces and lowering your blood sugar level.
Linagliptin comes as tablets you take once a day.
You'll usually need to take it long term. Do not stop taking it unless your doctor tells you to.
When taking linagliptin:
swallow the tablets whole with a glass of water (do not crush or chew them)
it's best to take it at the same time each day
you can take it with or without food
Always check the packet or leaflet that comes with your medicine. Ask a pharmacist or doctor for advice if you’re not sure how to take it or have any problems taking it.
If you miss a dose of linagliptin
If you forget to take a dose of linagliptin, take it as soon as you remember unless it's nearly time for your next dose.
If it's nearly time for your next dose, skip the dose you missed and take your next dose at the usual time.
Do not take 2 doses to make up for a missed dose.
Taking an extra dose of linagliptin can be dangerous.
Information
If you're told to go to A&E, do not drive. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.
Bring the linagliptin packet or leaflet inside it, any remaining medicine, and any other medicines you take.
you've taken more than your prescribed dose of linagliptin
Linagliptin can sometimes cause serious side effects, although most of them are rare.
Possible serious side effects of linagliptin include:
an allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) – causing symptoms such as a swollen throat or tongue, a raised, itchy rash or difficulty breathing
severe skin reactions – causing symptoms such as a sore, itchy, raised rash, blisters or peeling skin
swelling of your pancreas (pancreatitis) – causing symptoms such as severe pain in your stomach or your back that does not go away

cards.headline: Speak to a pharmacist or doctor if:

lines.text: you have any side effects that bother you or do not go away
They may be able to give you advice about how to reduce any side effects. Keep taking your medicine unless you're advised to stop.
you're taking linagliptin and think you might be having anaphylaxis, pancreatitis or serious skin reactions
If you think you're having any other serious side effect, call NHS 111.

cards.headline: Who can and cannot take linagliptin

lines.text: Most adults can take linagliptin, but it's not suitable for everyone.
For example, it may not be not suitable for you if:
you've had an allergic reaction or serious side effect from linagliptin or a similar medicine before
you've had pancreatitis or other problems with your pancreas
Before taking linagliptin, tell your doctor if you have any medical conditions.
Tell your doctor if you're breastfeeding.
Linagliptin is usually not used if you're breastfeeding. Your doctor may suggest stopping linagliptin or switching to a different medicine.
Tell your doctor if you're pregnant or get pregnant while taking linagliptin.
Linagliptin is not used during pregnancy. Your doctor may suggest stopping linagliptin or switching to a different medicine.

cards.headline: Taking linagliptin with other medicines, food and drink

lines.text: There are some medicines, remedies and supplements that may not mix well with linagliptin.
These include:
medicines to treat epilepsy or nerve pain, such as carbamazepine
rifampicin, a type of antibiotic
other medicines for high blood sugar, such as insulin, metformin or gliclazide – your doctor may want to change your dose of these medicines
Before taking linagliptin, tell your doctor if you're taking any other medicines, herbal remedies, vitamins or supplements.

Follow your doctor's advice about diet while taking linagliptin as part of your diabetes treatment to reduce the chances of your blood sugar level getting too low. This may include eating a healthy diet and not skipping or delaying meals.
It's best not to drink alcohol while taking linagliptin because it can affect your blood sugar level.
